comparison: Both address the main conclusions (C3-C9, C125) about c-di-AMP's role in developmental timing. OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED by comprehensive experimental evidence, while peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, stating 'the model proposed in the revised manuscript is still not fully supported by the data presented' and noting inconsistencies where similar c-di-AMP levels produce different phenotypes.

Both evaluate c-di-AMP measurements across engineered strains (C39-C48). OpenEval finds the ELISA data SUPPORTED with successful manipulation of c-di-AMP levels. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, extensively critiquing that 'only very high levels make a difference' and noting inconsistencies where strains with similar c-di-AMP levels (~256-300 pg/mL) show different phenotypes.

Both address phenotypic characterization of DacA overexpression strains (C50-C59 overlap with C53-C54, C57-C58, C97-C99). OpenEval finds comprehensive phenotypic data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'overexpression of DacA (cdiAMP ~4000 pg/ml) did not have a different phenotype than over expression of the mutant (cdiAMP ~256 pg/ml)' and that phenotypic effects don't consistently correlate with c-di-AMP levels.

Both evaluate dacA-KD strain characterization (C66-C73 overlap with C68-C69, C71-C72). OpenEval finds phenotypes SUPPORTED and consistent with impaired secondary differentiation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN as part of broader concerns about phenotype-c-di-AMP correlations, noting the model doesn't correctly predict growth rate changes.

Both address dacAop strain characterization (C78-C91 overlap with C82-C85). OpenEval finds contrasting phenotypes between dacAop and dacAopMut SUPPORTED as strong evidence for c-di-AMP's role. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting inconsistencies in the data and that effects don't cleanly support the proposed model.

Both evaluate time-course IFU assays showing EB production kinetics (C97-C100). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as key functional outcome linking c-di-AMP to developmental progression. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the model correctly predicts growth rate changes and noting phenotypic inconsistencies.

Both address membrane localization experiments comparing membrane-localized versus cytosolic DacA (C60-C65). OpenEval finds data SUPPORTED that membrane localization is critical for observed effects. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'Figure 3 shows no differences in anything measured although cdiAMP levels were again dramatically different' (~4000 vs ~1500 pg/mL), undermining clarity of whether effects are c-di-AMP-dependent or membrane-localization-dependent.

Both evaluate RT-qPCR data on premature hctA expression (C74-C77, with C76 overlap). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as key finding linking elevated c-di-AMP to earlier secondary differentiation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'complementation resulted in a moderate increase in hctA at a single time point but not at 24 hpi' and inconsistent effects on different late genes weaken support for the model.

Both address RNA-seq analysis of differential gene expression (C92-C96, with C92, C94 overlap). OpenEval finds comprehensive RNA-seq data SUPPORTED, providing genome-wide confirmation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting that overexpression 'increased hctA only at an early timepoint and not at 24hpi and again had no effect on omcB or euo,' with inconsistent effects weakening model support.

Both address the requirement for co-overexpression of DacA and YbbR (C49, C114-C115). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as reasonable inference that YbbR is the limiting factor. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the dramatic increases in c-di-AMP with co-overexpression, though they question broader implications for the developmental model.

Both evaluate the quantitative c-di-AMP threshold estimate (C38, C135). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as reasonable inference from comparing levels at different timepoints. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, noting strains with c-di-AMP around 300 pg/mL show effects while strains at 4000 pg/mL sometimes show no effects, and that 'only very high levels make a difference,' undermining the threshold model.

Both address c-di-AMP accumulation during developmental cycle (C25-C27, C37). OpenEval finds ELISA measurements SUPPORTED, confirming prior findings with clear statistical significance. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting this basic observation in wild-type conditions as foundational data, though questioning its interpretation within the broader model.

Both address the mechanistic model of c-di-AMP distribution and asymmetric division (C127-C134, with C130-C132 overlap). OpenEval finds the model SUPPORTED as consistent with data and plausible explanation for asynchronous differentiation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with their overall assessment that 'the data does not cleanly support the proposed model' applying to this mechanistic proposal, as fundamental issues with correlating c-di-AMP levels to phenotypes undermine plausibility.

Both address DacA localization (C50 overlap). OpenEval finds comprehensive phenotypic characterization including IFA SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED for the localization data itself, accepting this observational finding from immunofluorescence as accurately reported.

Both address colocalization analysis (C78 overlap). OpenEval finds comprehensive characterization including colocalization SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for the localization observation, not challenging this specific finding from the immunofluorescence experiments.

Both address DacA localization patterns (C107 overlap). OpenEval finds negative results (no septal localization) SUPPORTED and appropriately interpreted. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for localization data, accepting the observational findings from immunofluorescence.

Both address dominant-negative mechanism (C122-C124, with C123 overlap). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as reasonable mechanistic inference from differential effects of membrane-localized versus cytosolic mutants. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, as the observation that dramatically different c-di-AMP levels show no phenotypic differences in ΔTM constructs undermines clarity of the proposed mechanism.
